Two-step estimation of covariate effects in a two-level latent class model

twostep.Rd

The two-step estimator of Di Mari, Bakk, Oser and Kuha (2023) for two-level latent class and profile models (lca() / lpa() with level2 and KB): the measurement model of object (step 1, fitted without covariates) is held fixed, and the structural model – the between classes, P(CW | CB), within covariates of the individual class (cw ON x, slopes common to the between classes) and between covariates of the cluster class (cb ON z) – is estimated by maximum likelihood on the full two-level model (step 2). Covariates therefore cannot change what the classes mean.

Usage

twostep(
  object,
  data,
  covariates = NULL,
  between_covariates = NULL,
  se = c("corrected", "naive")
)

Arguments

object

A two-level latentmix model (level2, KB) fitted without covariates.

data

The data object was fitted to (same rows, same order).

covariates

Within (individual-level) covariates: columns of data (tidyselect) or a numeric data frame / matrix.

between_covariates

Cluster-level covariates, constant within each cluster.

se

"corrected" (default) or "naive".

Value

A two-level latentmix model of step 2 with the measurement model fixed (info$kind == "MLFIXED", classes labelled as in object): print it, or use coeftable() and parameters() for the class model with robust standard errors.

Details

se = "corrected" (default) corrects the step-2 standard errors for the estimation of the measurement model in step 1 (Bakk & Kuha 2018): V2 + I22^-1 I21 S1 I21' I22^-1, with the step-2 cluster sandwich V2, blocks of the observed information of the joint likelihood and the robust step-1 covariance S1. se = "naive" treats the measurement model as known; these agree with Mplus with the measurement parameters fixed. The corrected standard errors have no Mplus counterpart.

The bias-adjusted three-step alternative (Lyrvall, Bakk, Oser & Di Mari 2024) is r3step() on a two-level model; bch() gives BCH means of a within-level distal outcome by within class.

References

Di Mari, R., Bakk, Z., Oser, J., & Kuha, J. (2023). A two-step estimator for multilevel latent class analysis with covariates. Psychometrika, 88, 1144–1170.

Bakk, Z., & Kuha, J. (2018). Two-step estimation of models between latent classes and external variables. Psychometrika, 83, 871–892.

Lyrvall, J., Bakk, Z., Oser, J., & Di Mari, R. (2024). Bias-adjusted three-step multilevel latent class modeling with covariates. Structural Equation Modeling, 31, 592–603.

See also

r3step() (two-level three-step), bch(), lca()

Examples

data(schools)
# \donttest{
schools$female <- rep(0:1, length.out = nrow(schools))        # illustrative covariate
m <- lca(schools, starts_with("b_"), K = 3, level2 = school, KB = 2)
#> Starting Julia ...
ts <- twostep(m, schools, covariates = female)
coeftable(ts)
#>               kind class between         item         level    estimate
#> 1    between logit     0       1         CB#1       vs CB#2  0.60218915
#> 2 within intercept     1       0         CW#1       vs CW#3  0.24349564
#> 3 within intercept     2       0         CW#2       vs CW#3  0.27515545
#> 4     within slope     1       1 CW#1 ON CB#1 vs CW#3, CB#2  1.69978576
#> 5     within slope     2       1 CW#2 ON CB#1 vs CW#3, CB#2  0.98366297
#> 6 within covariate     1       0       female       CW#1 ON  0.02147866
#> 7 within covariate     2       0       female       CW#2 ON -0.13057618
#>          se          z            p oddsratio
#> 1 0.2754608  2.1861156 2.880715e-02 1.8261121
#> 2 0.2366197  1.0290590 3.034520e-01 1.2757007
